A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forecasting work, renamed from TianQuan-Climate to TianQuan-S2S. The main text, equations, rendered figures, tables, and appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ERA5 forecasting experiments, quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and appendix analyses of time series, prediction errors, and forecast correlations.

after.justification: v4 retains original forecasting results and reports additional baseline comparisons, ensemble-mean results, forecasting-strategy experiments, and intermediate-layer evaluations.

M1.justification: The reported central fusion operator changes: v1 Figure 4 specifies convolutional pixel attention with a sigmoid, whereas v4 Section 3.1 and Figure 2 construct fusion weights through learned query/key/value projections. The multi-model forecasting strategy, Fourier embeddings, noise-augmented Transformer, and latitude-weighted MSE remain; their renaming and expanded explanations are not separate method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions retain global ERA5 forecasting with the same variables and two spatial resolutions. v4 Appendix C additionally evaluates 5- and 10-day forecasts in Tables 7 and 9, modestly extending the evaluated horizons beyond v1's 15–45-day experiments. No additional geographic domain or weather dataset is established.

E2.justification: v4 adds evaluated FuXi-S2S comparisons to deterministic, ensemble, and case-study results, and adds XGBoost and Lasso in Table 11. Conversely, ClimaX is omitted from the component-ablation comparison in Table 3, and climatology disappears from the deterministic curves in Figure 3, although it participates in the new ensemble-mean comparison.

E3.justification: v4 introduces substantial additional evaluation designs: a scheduled-sampling autoregressive control, daily models using one input timestep versus five-day models using historical windows, and decoding intermediate Transformer blocks against several forecast horizons (Appendix C). It also adds ensemble-mean RMSE evaluation. The existing resolutions, optimizer, training schedule, and backbone configuration remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The climatology/noise component ablations are retained under revised names. v4 additionally tests autoregressive versus multi-model forecasting, one-day versus five-day model intervals, and claimed layer-to-lead-time alignment in Tables 7–9. The earlier appendix time-series, error-map, and multivariable scatter analyses remain as Figures 7–9; these are relocated material, not new analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports probabilistic metrics without specifying ensemble size or construction. v4 newly documents 50 randomly perturbed initial states plus an unperturbed control and averaging 51 forecasts. This adds stochastic-sampling information, without establishing an increase in runs. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v4 Table 1 expands v1 Table 2 with additional lead times and FuXi-S2S results, while revising retained entries: ClimaX's day-15 T850 CRPS changes from 2.821 to 2.831, and the proposed model's day-35 Z500 RQE changes from 674.2 to 705. Tables 2 and 7–11 add further results. The numerical revisions do not establish same-setting performance gains because v1 leaves ensemble construction unspecified.

T1.justification: v1 Section 3.4 develops a transport/diffusion PDE, its stochastic representation, and an Euler-discretization argument connecting it to the network. This mathematical development is removed rather than relocated in v4. The later version retains the stochastic residual update and Fourier/loss mathematics while introducing explicit query/key/value fusion equations.

C1.justification: The central claim that climatology fusion and a noise-augmented Transformer improve long-range forecasting remains. v4 explicitly extends its headline performance claims to both deterministic and ensemble forecasting against FuXi-S2S. The multi-model strategy, prominently claimed as a contribution in v1, is retained technically but no longer presented as a principal contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive interpretations about a short-range advantage for autoregression, the accuracy/cost tradeoff of model intervals, and alignment between Transformer depth and physical forecast lead time. It reframes noise through perturbed forecasting and variability preservation. v1's qualification about diminishing climatology-fusion benefits around 45 days disappears, while v4 discusses ensemble wind forecasts losing to climatology.

D1.justification: v4 newly specifies training/validation/test years, the 1979–2016 climatology window, ensemble construction, FuXi forecast sourcing, sampling times, wind-speed processing, and additional inference details. These substantially expand documentation without proving changes to existing experiments. Hyperparameters and hardware are retained, while some explicit convolution-kernel specifications and the RE/SI formulas provided in v1 are omitted.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning through perturbed forecasting, newer weather models, and subseasonal research, adding references such as SwinVRNN, CirT, Aurora, and Aardvark Weather. FuXi-S2S was already cited in v1, but v4 adds a substantive architectural contrast concerning latent perturbations versus layerwise noise and explicit climatology. References supporting the removed PDE argument disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, and results narrative are extensively rewritten. v4 adds Preliminaries, moves related work after experiments, consolidates method subsections, and expands the appendix organization with notation and inference sections plus a contents page. The model/title renaming and author-list edits accompany this broader restructuring.

P2.justification: v4 redesigns the motivation and architecture figures, rearranges the deterministic plots, expands ensemble tables, and replaces grouped ablation bars with a numerical table. Forecast maps and the main scatter comparison gain FuXi-S2S panels. The multi-model diagram moves to the appendix, and the main text changes from two-column to single-column layout; several appendix graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 strengthens empirical support through FuXi-S2S comparisons and a direct autoregressive control for the previously untested strategy choice, while making splits and ensemble construction more explicit. These gains are tempered by removing the deterministic climatology curves and the associated horizon qualification. New preprocessing documentation also conflicts internally: Appendix D.4 describes averaging four sampled times, but its equations average 24 samples. The revision therefore provides a limited net quality improvement, with material reproducibility and qualification problems remaining.
